question.text: Let $(v, w)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $v+w?$ \[ \begin{cases} 0.4v-2w=2\\ v-w=1 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the top equation by $10,$ as follows:

\[ \begin{cases} 0.4v-2w=2 & \Big| \: \times 10 \\ v-w=1 & \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} 4v-20w=20 \\ v-w=1 \end{cases} \]

Notice that if we multiply the second equation by $-4,$ then we will get a $-4v$ term that can cancel with the $4v$ term in the first equation:

\[ \begin{cases} 4v-20w=20 & \\ v-w=1 & \Big| \: \times (-4) \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} 4v-20w=20 \\ -4v+4w=-4 \end{cases} \]

Adding the two equations eliminates the $v$-variable and allows us to solve for $w\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \cancel{4v}-20w&=20\\ -\cancel{4v}+4w&=-4\\[3pt] \hline (-20w+4w) &= (20-4)\\[3pt] -16w &= 16 \\[3pt] w &= -1 \end{align*}

Finally, we can substitute $w=-1$ into the equation $v-w=1$ to solve for $v\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} v-w&=1 \\[3pt] v - (-1) &= 1 \\[3pt] v + 1 &= 1 \\[3pt] v &= 0 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $v=0, \,w=-1.$ So,

\[ v+w=0 + (-1) = -1. \]

example.title: Solving a System Containing Decimals in One Equation

question.text:
Let $(a, b)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $a+b?$

\[ \begin{cases} 0.4a-0.8b-1.2=0\\ 0.5a-1.5b-5=0 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $10,$ as follows:

\[ \begin{cases} 0.4a-0.8b-1.2=0 & \Big| \: \times 10 \\[2pt] 0.5a-1.5b-5=0 & \Big| \: \times 10 \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} 4a-8b-12=0 \\[2pt] 5a-15b-50=0 \end{cases} \]

Notice that if we divide the first equation by $4$ and the second equation by $-5,$ we will get a $a$ term in the first equation that can cancel with the $-a$ term in the second equation:

\[ \begin{cases} 4a-8b-12=0 & \Big| \: \div (4) \\ 5a-15b-50=0 & \Big| \: \div (-5) \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} a-2b-3=0 \\ -a+3b+10=0 \end{cases} \]

Adding the two equations eliminates the $a$-variable and allows us to solve for $b\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \require{cancel} \cancel{a}-2b-3&=0 \\ -\cancel{a}+3b+10&=0 \\[3pt] \hline (-2b+3b)+(-3+10)&= 0\\[3pt] b+7&=0\\[3pt] b&=-7 \end{align}

Finally, we can substitute $b=-7$ into the equation $a-2b-3=0$ to solve for $a\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} a-2b-3&=0 \\[3pt] a-2(-7)-3&=0\\[3pt] a+14-3&=0\\[3pt] a+11&=0\\[3pt] a &=-11 \end{align}

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-11$ and $b=-7.$ So, \[ a+b=-11+(-7)=-18. \]

example.title: Solving a System Containing Decimals in Both Equations

question.explanation:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $10,$ as follows:

\[ \begin{cases} 3.5a-4.5b-8=0 & \Big| \: \times 10 \\[2pt] 0.6a-1.2b-1.8=0 & \Big| \: \times 10 \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} 35a-45b-80=0 \\[2pt] 6a-12b-18=0 \end{cases} \]

Notice that we can solve for $a$ in the second equation:

\begin{align*} 6a-12b-18 &= 0 \\[5pt] 6a &= 12b+18 \\[5pt] a &= \dfrac{12b+18}{6} \\[5pt] a&= 2b+3 \end{align*}

Now, to find the value of $b,$ we can substitute $a=2b+3$ into the first equation:

\begin{align*} 35a-45b-80 &=0 \\[3pt] 35(2b+3) - 45b -80 &= 0 \\[3pt] 70b+105-45b-80 &= 0 \\[3pt] 25b+25 &= 0 \\[3pt] 25b &= -25 \\[3pt] b&=-1 \end{align*}

Finally, we substitute $b=-1$ into the equation $a=2b+3$ to get:

\begin{align*} a &=2b+3 \\[3pt] a &= 2(-1)+3 \\[3pt] a &= -2+3 \\[3pt] a &= 1 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=1, \,b=-1.$
